newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Top N.Korean defector's son detained - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Top N.Korean defector's son detained - newspaper.

text.p: A top North Korean defector's son was detained by police in the communist country as he attempted to flee to China, a South Korean daily reported on Wednesday.

The Dong-a Ilbo quoted a South Korean official saying that a recent defector testified that people close to Hwang Jang-yop said Hwang and main members of Hwang's political circle were purged or sent to political prison camps following the defection of Pyongyang's top ideologue.
Hwang's son, fearing for his life, attempted an escape, but was caught near the border near China, the official was quoted as saying.
The Dong-a Ilbo made no indication as to how the defector obtained this information.
Family members of defectors in the North often face execution or are taken to prison camps.

Hwang sought asylum at South Korea's Beijing consulate in February, and after more than two months in China and the Philippines, arrived in Seoul in April. He is the highest ranking official ever to defect to the South.
The Dong-a, a major South Korean daily, said the official identified the defector as a 41-year-old North Korean acupuncturist who secretly fled to the South through the Czech Republic last month.

The defector, a graduate of Pyongyang's premier medical school for the elite, was sent to the Czech Republic to raise foreign exchange for the cash-strapped Stalinist country. He decided to flee to the South after listening to the British Broadcasting Corporation's radio reports, the newspaper said.

He also testified that the North Korean government was assuaging its military leaders of Hwang's defection by saying "Hwang Jang-yop was a secretary in charge of ideology and knows nothing about the military, so do not worry".

The defector also said he heard through his medical circle that North Korean leader Kim Jong-il "overall had no health problems" but "has complained of pain in the back of his neck resulting from stress".

He added that North Korea sent three physicians to Switzerland for cardiac research in case Kim Jong-il suffers a heart attack. Kim's father, the "Great Leader" Kim Il-sung died in 1994 reportedly from a heart attack.
South and North Korea are still techincally at war as the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a truce and not a peace agreement.
